Trying to run Linux Mint on 2nd internal hard drive

It should be no problem generally. You need to check which disk it boots from and put the bootloader there. For some distros you also need to disable UEFI secure boot if it is enabled.

The installer will ask about partitioning, make sure to put the new partition on the right disk.

You can skip messing with the bootloader and dual boot settings and just do it manually with a couple of sata drive bays like this. Then you don't have to risk something going wrong with your main OS, and you have a test drive you can screw around with and learn on.

1. Create and boot from Linux Mint Installation disk (you should be able to find instructions online, let me know if you have questions to this point).
  2. When everything loads, click on "Install Linux Mint" icon on the desktop.
  3. Pick your language, etc.
  4. When it asks how you want to install, select the last option, 'something else'.
  5. A confusing screen will appear with things like sda sdb etc listed. You want to click on the one that is your 128GB SSD. So it will be listed as something like 'sbd 128000'.
  6. You then have to click the little + sign and select ext4, click the 'format' box, and select "/" from the dropdown menu. Then continue. Ignore the stuff about swapspace.
  7. The rest should be easy.

This is mostly from memory, but those were the parts I got confused at. You can boot from the dvd and open firefox to view this page while installing.
